chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that

the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered upon a man from the Clan of Hashim who was in the throes of death. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Say:

There is no god except Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. There is no god except Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and all that is between them, and Lord of the Magnificent Throne. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
So he said it, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Praise be to Allah Who rescued him from the Fire.'

key_terms.اسْتَنْقَذَ: istanqadha — to rescue or save; here Allah rescued the man from the Fire through his recitation of the dhikr
key_terms.التَّلْقِين: talqeen — the Islamic practice of instructing a dying person with specific remembrances and the declaration of faith
key_terms.يَقْضِي: expiring/in the throes of death — the Arabic term yaqdi (from qada') is a classical euphemism for the act of dying

ai.seo_question: What dhikr did the Prophet Muhammad teach a dying man from Banu Hashim according to Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) visited a dying man from the Hashimite clan and instructed him to recite a specific dhikr (remembrance of Allah) combining the declaration of divine unity with glorification of Allah as the Forbearing, Generous, and the Lord of all creation. When the man recited the dhikr, the Prophet praised Allah for rescuing him from the Fire. This narration is cited in the chapter on talqeen (instruction of the dying), reflecting the Shia practice of guiding believers at the moment of death with words of tawhid and divine glorification, understood as a spiritual protection against hellfire.
